title: On Cognitive Debt and the Care of the Habitat
summary: Introduces cognitive debt as the gap between what a system is and what teams collectively understand it to be, distinct from technical debt; proposes habitat thinking and practices like externalizing intent, optimizing for re-entry, and introducing environmental sensors (re-explanation friction, bus-factor confidence, time-to-comprehension metrics) to detect and prevent understanding erosion before it causes systemic collapse.
when-to-read: Read this when you're concerned about hidden knowledge silos, team confusion during incidents, or velocity that masks shallow understanding—particularly in teams adopting AI-assisted coding. If you're looking for concrete metrics on code quality or testing approaches, consult the code-quality or testing tags instead; this article focuses on the human comprehension side of maintainability.
